principles: Discovery is not authority: a policy response may describe requirements but cannot become a receipt, signature, gate pass, or evidence acceptance.
Keep koala authority enforce isolated from ordinary Koala workflow commands so existing thin-client behavior remains stable.
Prefer typed contracts and focused smokes over natural-language claims about safety.
Fail closed on malformed, unreachable, or overclaiming authority policy responses.
Leave M2+ responsibilities explicit instead of implementing actor, runner, evidence, or receipt behavior early.
drivers: Python authority already owns authority-policy.v1 and its compatibility fields.
Users need a safe local command to inspect production requirements before enforcing them.
Existing Koala flow forgery protections rely on not confusing transport acceptance with receipt-backed authority.

options.name: OPT-A
pros: Easy to test without network side effects
cons: Does not yet make Koala CLI a production enforce runner
Users still need Python authority and Mac Runner integration later

options.name: OPT-B
pros: Would deliver actor registration, job claiming, evidence, and receipt checks in one story
cons: Too much blast radius for a single milestone
High risk of blurring discovery and authority
Harder to verify without Python and Mac changes

options.name: OPT-C
cons: Does not advance enforce subsystem mechanics beyond B-7e38

rationale: Choose OPT-A because Milestone 1 should give operators a mechanically testable read-only compatibility check while preserving the B-7e38 boundary that only Python authority receipts can confer production authority.

preMortem.scenario: Policy discovery output is mistaken for a gate pass.
preMortem.trigger: The command prints accepted or receipt-like wording, or the schema allows receipt/gate fields.
preMortem.consequence: Agent can cite a discovery response as proof of authority.
preMortem.mitigation: Reject or flag receipt, receiptId, gatePassed, and accepted fields; print discovery-only warning in every success output.

preMortem.scenario: New command accidentally submits local evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation reuses submitEvidence or evidence-flow handler code paths.
preMortem.consequence: M1 crosses into M2+ trust boundary without receipts/signatures.
preMortem.mitigation: Use GET /v1/authority/policy only, add smoke fetch spy that fails on POST /v1/evidence and /v1/evidence/batch.

preMortem.scenario: Nested command shape breaks existing flat Koala CLI dispatch.
preMortem.trigger: Only implementing koala authority enforce policy without a registry command or phase policy entry.
preMortem.consequence: Command is unusable or unclassified by ownership policy.
preMortem.mitigation: Register flat authority_enforce_policy and optionally normalize nested argv alias to that command; add command ownership smoke coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Policy schema is too loose to catch malformed production compatibility data.
preMortem.consequence: Operators see success for an unusable policy payload.
preMortem.mitigation: Require contractVersion, purpose, supported modes, compatibility, digests, and evidencePolicy preset; malformed responses return non-success.
